# Parking Lot + Robotaxi Dispatch

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/sd-parking-and-dispatch)** — free, no card: the interview workspace, an AI interviewer to push back on your design, and the reference solution.

## Problem

## Requirements

- Design a model for an AV depot with N parking locations. A subset supports charging, another subset consists of maintenance bays, and every remaining location is an idle parking spot.
- Describe how vehicles move through the lifecycle `in-service → idle → charging → maintenance → idle`, accounting for minimum or required dwell periods and limited resources.
- At the depot exit, arriving riders must be assigned to the next suitable vehicle. The assignment policy should reduce rider waiting time without compromising fleet condition, including battery health and maintenance timing.
- Identify the metrics that drive operational decisions and order them by importance.

## Notes

## Preparation

- Start with the state model, then define dispatch behavior, and only afterward select metrics. A frequent mistake in this kind of design exercise is proposing dispatch before the vehicle states are explicitly defined.
- Prepare and prioritize 3–4 measurements in each group—rider, fleet, and system—because interviewers commonly ask which metric should be optimized first.
- Review an applied article about ride-hailing dispatch to become familiar with cost-function terminology.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Model the depot as a state machine where each vehicle transitions through states (in-service, idle, charging, maintenance) with constraints on dwell times and resource availability.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a priority queue or scheduling algorithm to assign vehicles to charging or maintenance slots based on their state and urgency, and dispatch idle vehicles to service requests.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Handle the lifecycle by tracking each vehicle's battery level, maintenance schedule, and location, and use a centralized dispatcher to optimize for minimal wait time and resource utilization.

</details>
